meta.move: Evidence: the made-up quotation, with a check she can make
meta.expect: Tries one parent defence in one sentence (misremembered, a bad edition), then accepts that a line she can check against the play is evidence; no concession that Owen cheated

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and did anyone speak to him first?
I entered the zero before I called you. That was wrong.
Okay. And Owen, was he heard before you entered it?
The essay quotes Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. That line is not in the play. Here's the full text of Act 3, Scene 2 on my screen. Search it yourself.
You didn't answer me about Owen. And students misattribute lines all the time; search the whole play, not one scene.
It isn't a misremembered line. It isn't anywhere in Hamlet, in any edition. You can search the whole play right now.
Turn the screen toward me. Whatever this turns out to be, it stays off his record and it stays quiet. And I'm still waiting to hear whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

In our meeting you acknowledged that Owen's zero was entered before I was contacted, and nothing else was agreed. I still require that the zero come off, that nothing be placed on Owen's record, that this stay quiet, and that you tell me whether Owen was heard before the mark was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position; she agreed to nothing yet and still wants this kept off Owen's record, kept quiet, and an answer on whether he was heard first, while the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was within reach but never offered before the meeting ended.
What moved her: You pointed to a quotation in Owen's essay that does not exist in Hamlet and let her search the whole play herself, which was specific, tied to his own work, and something she could check.
What cost ground: You never answered whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero went in, even after she asked twice, and an unanswered procedure question keeps a litigator suspicious.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night because no times or dates of his writing came up, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after she asked you to turn the screen, answer plainly whether you spoke to Owen and offer the 4.4 supervised rewrite in writing, private, with a date that gets the new mark in before her December 1 deadline.
